data.caption: ENGO® 2 Photochromic - Real time data for endurance athletes | Engo Eyewear | Engo Eyewear
data.copy:
Here's all you need to know on devices joining the ENGO party 💪:
✔️ Mobile App: Available for iOS, Android devices 📱
✔️ Garmin Datafield: for 100+ select devices (see below). ⌚
✔️ Apple Watch App: Any recent Apple Watch running watchOS 10.1 or higher (connects through the ActiveLook iOS app extension).
✔️ SuuntoPlus : All Suunto 9, Suunto 5 and more (feature set = 1 metric dashboard + navigation)

⌚ Here’s a deeper dive on Garmin :
- Over 100 Garmin devices are supported, including most mid- to high-end models in the Edge, Fenix, Forerunner, Quatix, Marq, Epix, Tactix, and Venu series (and more!). 
- ENGO works with all devices powerful enough to run the ActiveLook Datafield app.
- The compatibility list is constantly updated as new Garmin products launch. Find the latest version on http://engoeyewear.com

🔎 What about Coros, Polar, Hammerhead, Wahoo, Whoop, or other fitness trackers ?
- They aren't officially supported (yet!) but, you can still experience ENGO.. with your smartphone
- Simply use the ActiveLook app for iOS or Android: It connects to your heart rate monitor, bike sensors, or running pod, providing all key metrics to adjust your intensity. Accuracy Note: Precision on pace, speed, and distance will depend on your phone's GPS quality.
- Looking Ahead: Adding more platforms requires collaboration with the device manufacturers themselves. And we're actively discussing and developing with some brands!
-Want to see ENGO on your favorite device? Let the manufacturer know! Your voice can make a difference.

🚀Beyond Cycling and Running?
- ENGO leverages the ActiveLook platform, open to all developpers. It therefore supports many other apps and devices!
- This includes rowing, sailing, paragliding, speech to text, navigation, and even model airplane control! ‍⛵🪂️✈️ (Yes, really!)
- Curious? Check the ActiveLook website to explore the possibilities!

Stay tuned for more updates on ENGO !

data.caption: I Knew It on Day Two. I Have Seen Where This Goes...
data.copy:
I knew on day two.

Not because it hurt that bad yet. Because I recognized it.

The way you recognize a song from the first three notes. The way you recognize a face you wish you didn't know.

My left shoulder. A pull. A catch. Something slightly off when I reached for my coffee mug.

I stood at the kitchen counter and I just... knew.

I've had frozen shoulder before. Right side. Eighteen months of my life. A year and a half of sleeping in a recliner, of doing my bra in front and spinning it around like a child, of watching my husband try not to notice that I needed help with everything.

Eighteen months to get my arm back.

And now here I am again. Different shoulder. Same opening move.

I didn't tell my husband right away. I stood there with my coffee and I ran through the timeline in my head. Freezing phase. Frozen phase. Thawing. Eighteen months minimum. Maybe two years. Maybe permanent loss if I'm unlucky.

I know this road. I've memorized it.

That's why the second one scared me more than the first.

If you're reading this and you've had it in one shoulder and you feel something starting in the other one... you already know what I mean.

That specific kind of dread. It's not even pain yet. It's the knowledge of what's coming. It's having seen the whole movie and sitting down to watch it again.

40% of women get it in both shoulders. I read that AFTER my second one started.

Nobody warned me. Not my GP. Not my orthopedic surgeon. Not the physical therapist who told me to "be patient" with my first one.

Nobody said: by the way, there's nearly a coin-flip chance this happens again on the other side.

I would have done something differently. I would have done SOMETHING. Anything. I would not have just waited.

So I want to tell you what I spent on my first frozen shoulder. Because you need to understand what "waiting it out" actually costs.

$1,800 on physical therapy. Ten sessions. It made it worse. I know that now, but at the time I kept going because what else…

data.caption: hatchingtime.com
data.copy:
Soooo I just wanted to provide an update on the @hatchingtime (link in bio) quail home.
•
DISCLAIMER: If you don’t like this setup (for whatever reason) this post is not for you. All of my content won’t be for everyone. However, if you are an urban dweller or live in a place where raising your own meat is not doable outside this maybe helpful. I absolutely could raise my quail outside and on the ground but my body is no longer a fan. Also, if you aren’t new here you know my quail were never pets. They are for meat and eggs. However, they are still well taken care of and treated well. There is no overcrowding, the cages are kept clean, they always have food and water and they also get treats. Wanted to get that out of the way first. Have had unfollow announcements 😒 and judgmental comments across platforms related to this setup. I’m not here telling anyone what to do or that what they are doing is wrong, I’m simply sharing my urban homesteading journey. I had made a decision that I wasn’t going to post about the quail anymore but then I decided someone may need this information so here we go 😂.
•
Now, let’s get to the real point of this post lol. First, the thing I’m most excited about…I was able to integrate two quail using this system with zero issues! Literally no fighting at all! You know my integration efforts in the past have been stressful. The system has proven to be less work and has lowered the amount of food waste as well. There is no fighting in any covey (there are three quail in each cage) and they all healthy. I was going to say happy and healthy but the truth is they cannot talk to say if they are or are not so we are keeping this post real and honest. However, none of them are showing signs of stress so that gives me relief.
•
Anywho, I just wanted to share in case someone is trying to figure out how they maybe able to raise their own meat inside. This is a viable option but it’s not the only option! Do your own resear…

data.caption: I Knew It on Day Two. I Have Seen Where This Goes...
data.copy:
I knew on day two.

Not because it hurt that bad yet. Because I recognized it.

The way you recognize a song from the first three notes. The way you recognize a face you wish you didn't know.

My left shoulder. A pull. A catch. Something slightly off when I reached for my coffee mug.

I stood at the kitchen counter and I just... knew.

I've had frozen shoulder before. Right side. Eighteen months of my life. A year and a half of sleeping in a recliner, of doing my bra in front and spinning it around like a child, of watching my husband try not to notice that I needed help with everything.

Eighteen months to get my arm back.

And now here I am again. Different shoulder. Same opening move.

I didn't tell my husband right away. I stood there with my coffee and I ran through the timeline in my head. Freezing phase. Frozen phase. Thawing. Eighteen months minimum. Maybe two years. Maybe permanent loss if I'm unlucky.

I know this road. I've memorized it.

That's why the second one scared me more than the first.

If you're reading this and you've had it in one shoulder and you feel something starting in the other one... you already know what I mean.

That specific kind of dread. It's not even pain yet. It's the knowledge of what's coming. It's having seen the whole movie and sitting down to watch it again.

40% of women get it in both shoulders. I read that AFTER my second one started.

Nobody warned me. Not my GP. Not my orthopedic surgeon. Not the physical therapist who told me to "be patient" with my first one.

Nobody said: by the way, there's nearly a coin-flip chance this happens again on the other side.

I would have done something differently. I would have done SOMETHING. Anything. I would not have just waited.

So I want to tell you what I spent on my first frozen shoulder. Because you need to understand what "waiting it out" actually costs.

$1,800 on physical therapy. Ten sessions. It made it worse. I know that now, but at the time I kept going because what else…
